text:
morgan: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard flagged a ~9% p95 latency regression on canary after the merge that rolled at 00:30 UTC. Canaries are blocked. :eyes:

jia: saw it too. metrics show the bump only for short-seq workloads (~32 tokens). long sequences unchanged.

sam: any obvious kernel-selector deltas in the deploy?

morgan: the merge touched kernel selector heuristics + a batching window tweak (PR #8473). I ran a quick grep:

```
commit 3a9f7c2 PR#8473 runtime/kernel_selector: prefer fused-attn for seq<=64
commit e5b1c8d runtime/batcher: reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 4
```

harpreet: interesting — fused-attn is faster for single large batch but we saw a throughput drop under frequent small-batch traffic last week. Could be wrong kernel path choice causing more kernel switches.

morgan: profiling supports that: on canary trace, there's extra context-switch and more kernel load calls. snippet from perf profiler: `kernel_select_time_ms` doubled for short seqs.

ci-bot: nightly-regression: canary-p95-latency +9.2% (baseline vs current); alerts triggered @1765432060.

jia: agree we should bisect quickly. @sam can you run a targeted revert of the kernel-selector flag in staging and trigger the same load?

sam: on it. spinning up a staging canary with kernel-selector reverted and batching wait restored to 8ms. will push traffic replay of short-seq suite.

harpreet: while that's running, I wonder if KV cache behavior amplified it — short sequences hit cached KV more, and we might be thrashing caches when kernel path changes cause different KV layout. check eviction metrics?

morgan: eviction spike correlates with the time of merge on canary: `kv_evictions_per_min` tripled for the host group.

sam: staging replay complete. results: p95 back to baseline when kernel-selector is reverted, batching wait change alone had ~1% impact. Looks like kernel selection is main culprit.

jia: thanks. can we do a narrow revert (just the selector heuristic) to unblock canary rollout now? We should keep the batching wait tweak in review — may be harmless or beneficial separately.

morgan: created revert PR #8490 (revert kernel-selector change). marking rollout blocked -> awaiting revert merge.

ops-bot: rollback required: revert PR#8490 created by morgan. Executors: eng-runtime oncall.

harpreet: quick follow-up: we should add a microbenchmark that simulates high qps short-seq traffic to catch this in CI perf. current CI test uses longer sequences. I'll propose a small harness.

sam: agreed. also add an assertion in nightly dashboard comparing kernel_select_time_ms for seq buckets so we get more visibility next time.

morgan: TL;DR — kernel-selector heuristic caused p95 spike on short sequences; revert posted and canary rollout blocked until revert lands; next steps: add CI microbenchmark + dashboard bucket checks + postmortem once resolved. :thumbsup:
